effects: The signer sends exactly `assets` PYUSD to the vault (safeTransferFrom from msg.sender).
The vault mints previewDeposit(assets) shares to `onBehalf`; the share count comes from the vault price in storage, and the call has no minimum.
Before the deposit, accrueInterest mints fee shares to the fee recipients, which sets the share price the signer gets.
formats.shown: Deposit 2 PYUSD for an address, with the share ticker as a constant and the share recipient; the number of shares is not shown.

findings.title: deposit shows the share ticker 'senPYUSDmain', but the vault token's on-chain symbol is senPYUSDV2.
findings.evidence: descriptor metadata.constants.vaultTicker = "senPYUSDmain"; case 0 mined: the signer receives asset 0xb576…fb2 with symbol "senPYUSDV2". The adapter also mints a different token "senPYUSD" (0x19b3…), so a similar ticker can confuse the signer.
findings.fix: Set vaultTicker to the on-chain symbol "senPYUSDV2", or use a tokenAmount-style reference to @.to instead of a raw constant.

findings.title: deposit does not show how many shares the signer receives, and the code sets no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);` The shares come from the storage price, and there is no minShares parameter. In case 0 the signer received 1.001 senPYUSDV2, and the screen did not show this.

cases.notes: The screen shows 2 PYUSD out right. The screen gives the share asset (with another ticker) and the recipient, but no amount and no bound.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns previewWithdraw(assets) shares from `onBehalf`, rounded up, with no maximum in the call.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, the call spends the signer's share allowance from `onBehalf`.
The vault sends exactly `assets` PYUSD to `receiver`.
Before the withdrawal, accrueInterest mints fee shares to the fee recipients, which sets the share price.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly N PYUSD to the receiver, from the owner; the shares burned are not shown.

findings.title: withdraw does not show the shares burned from the owner, and the call has no maximum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);` with deleteShares(onBehalf, shares). In case 2 the signer lost 65.893 senPYUSDV2, and the screen did not show this.

cases.notes: The screen shows 131.634892 PYUSD in to the signer. The reader knew shares leave but not how many.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns exactly `shares` vault shares from `onBehalf`; when the signer is not the owner, this spends the signer's share allowance.
The vault sends previewRedeem(shares) PYUSD to `receiver`; the amount comes from the storage price, and the call has no minimum.
Before the redemption, accrueInterest mints fee shares to the fee recipients, which sets the payout.
formats.shown: Redeem N shares to the receiver, from the owner; the screen does not name the asset received or its amount.

findings.title: redeem never names PYUSD as the asset the receiver gets, although the asset is fixed and the descriptor can show it.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);` The redeem format has only shares, receiver and owner fields. In case 3 the signer received 655,731.180954 PYUSD. The reader was unsure: 'Whether the payout token is PYUSD'.
findings.fix: Add a field {"label":"Receive asset","format":"raw","value":"$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"}, as the mint format does. Change interpolatedIntent to "Redeem {#.shares} for PYUSD to {#.receiver}".

findings.title: redeem does not show the PYUSD amount received, and the call sets no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);` The price comes from storage, and there is no minAssets parameter.

findings.title: redeem shows the shares as senPYUSDmain, but the token's on-chain symbol is senPYUSDV2.
findings.evidence: case 3 screen: '328223.810274430875386736 senPYUSDmain'; mined: the signer sends asset 0xb576…fb2 with symbol "senPYUSDV2".
findings.fix: Align the ticker with the on-chain symbol senPYUSDV2.

cases.notes: The screen shows the shares out right. The reader guessed PYUSD in but did not know the asset or the amount.

effects: The signer sends previewMint(shares) PYUSD to the vault, rounded up; the amount comes from the storage price, and the call has no maximum.
The vault mints exactly `shares` shares to `onBehalf`.
Before the mint, accrueInterest mints fee shares to the fee recipients, which sets the price.
formats.shown: Mint N shares for the recipient, with 'Deposit asset: PYUSD' as a constant and no PYUSD amount.

findings.title: mint does not show the PYUSD amount taken from the signer, and the call has no maximum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);` and enter: `safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)`. In case 1, 1 unit of PYUSD left the signer, and the screen showed no amount.

findings.title: mint's interpolated intent omits that the signer pays PYUSD; only a separate constant field says so.
findings.evidence: interpolatedIntent "Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}"; the field 'Deposit asset' is a raw constant 'PYUSD'. In case 1, PYUSD left the signer.
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to "Pay PYUSD to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}".

findings.title: mint shows the minted shares as senPYUSDmain, but the on-chain symbol is senPYUSDV2.
findings.evidence: case 1 screen: '0.000000001 senPYUSDmain'; mined: the vault mints token 0xb576…fb2 with symbol senPYUSDV2.
findings.fix: Align the ticker with the on-chain symbol senPYUSDV2.

cases.notes: The screen names PYUSD out to the vault but gives no amount and no bound. The shares go to 0xdead, which is not the signer.
